q: 文章区分了哪两类 hot key 问题？（多选）
q_en: Which two hot-key problems does this cache design distinguish? (multi-select)
options: hot reads：某些 key 被大量读取
hot writes：某些 key 被大量并发写入
hot schemas：DDL 太频繁
hot TLS：证书过热
options_en: Hot reads: some keys receive very high read traffic.
Hot writes: some keys receive many concurrent writes.
Hot schemas: DDL changes too often.
Hot TLS: certificates overheating.
why: 读热点和写热点缓解手段不同：读靠复制分摊，写常靠批处理或拆分，混在一起容易选错方案。
why_en: Hot reads and hot writes need different fixes — replication spreads reads, while batching or sharding handles writes — so conflating them leads to the wrong fix.
optionExplanations: 对：读热点是本文讨论的两类问题之一。
对：写热点是另一类，并发更新集中在一个 key。
错：DDL 频率是数据库运维话题，不是缓存的 hot key 问题。
错：这不是一个真实存在的技术术语，纯粹跑题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: hot reads are one of the two hot-key categories discussed.
Correct: hot writes are the other — concentrated concurrent updates on one key.
Incorrect: DDL frequency is a database-ops topic, not a cache hot-key issue.
Incorrect: this isn't a real technical term — pure distraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层加密协议，用于建立安全连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS is a transport-layer protocol used to establish an encrypted connection.

scenario: 线上单 shard CPU 打满：一个 viral 视频 key 被狂读，另一个计数器 key 被狂写。
scenario_en: One shard is pinned at full CPU: a viral video key is being hammered by reads while a counter key is hammered by writes.

q: 对 hot read，简单升级所有节点硬件的问题是什么？
q_en: For a hot read, what is wrong with simply upgrading every node?
options: 扩容后一致性哈希的虚拟节点映射会全部失效
为几个热 key 给全集群花钱，没治根因
内存变大之后 TTL 的过期检查会跟着失效
升级硬件会强制把所有写入都改成同步复制
options_en: After the upgrade, all consistent-hashing virtual-node mappings break.
You pay for the whole cluster because of a few hot keys, without fixing the root cause.
With more memory, TTL expiry checks stop working.
Upgrading hardware forces every write into synchronous replication.
why: 热点通常集中在少数 key 或 shard，给所有节点扩容是线性烧钱，也扛不住热点继续增长。
why_en: Hot spots usually concentrate on a few keys or shards, so upgrading every node scales cost linearly and still can't outrun a growing hotspot.
optionExplanations: 错：升级硬件和路由算法无关，一致性哈希照常工作。
对：为少数热点全局加钱，性价比差且不解决根因。
错：升级硬件不影响过期逻辑，TTL 照常生效。
错：升级硬件不改变复制策略，同步与否是独立决定。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: upgrading hardware is unrelated to the routing algorithm; consistent hashing is unaffected.
Correct: paying globally for a few hot keys is poor value and misses the root cause.
Incorrect: upgrading hardware doesn't touch expiry logic; TTL still works.
Incorrect: upgrading hardware doesn't change replication strategy, which is a separate decision.
scenario: 50 个节点的缓存里只有 3 个 key 把单个 shard 压垮了，扩容预算有限。
scenario_en: In a 50-node cache just three keys are crushing one shard, and the budget for more hardware is limited.

scenario: 某个商品或 viral 内容的 key 有 100k read/s，但写入很少；单 shard 被读流量打爆。
scenario_en: A product or viral-content key gets 100k reads per second but very few writes, and its shard is overloaded by read traffic.
q: 最有针对性的缓存内缓解方案是什么？
q_en: What is the most targeted mitigation inside the cache?
options: 直接把这个热 key 从缓存中删除，等下次访问再重建
把整个集群全部节点都改成同步复制，指望它顺便分摊读压力
给 hot key 建多个带后缀的副本，读随机选一份
让所有相关请求统一排队等待 1 分钟后再处理
options_en: Delete the hot key from the cache and let it be rebuilt on the next access.
Switch every node in the cluster to synchronous replication, hoping it also spreads read load.
Create several suffixed copies of the hot key and let reads pick one at random.
Queue every related request for a full minute before processing.
tradeoff: 读负载分摊 vs 写入要同步更新所有副本
why: 只复制热点 key 比复制整台节点更精准，读流量能摊到多个节点；写入要更新所有副本，因此最适合读多写少。
why_en: Replicating just the hot key is more targeted than replicating a whole node, spreading reads across copies at the cost of updating every copy on a write.
whenOtherWins: 若热点是整类数据或地域问题，专用 hot-key tier 或 CDN 式层更合适；写热点不适合这种多副本方案。
diagram:
flowchart LR
HotKey[Hot read key] --> Promote[Promote replicas]
Promote --> R1[Replica A]
Promote --> R2[Replica B]
Promote --> R3[Replica C]
Client[Clients] --> R1
Client --> R2
Client --> R3
optionExplanations: 错：删除 key 会导致业务数据在重建前不可用，不是缓解手段。
错：同步复制会让所有写都变慢，跟这里的读热点无关。
对：后缀副本分散到不同节点，读随机选副本分摊压力。
错：排队 1 分钟会让用户体验直接崩溃，不是真实方案。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: deleting the key leaves it unavailable until rebuilt — not a mitigation.
Incorrect: synchronous replication slows every write and doesn't address this read hotspot.
Correct: suffixed copies spread across nodes let reads randomly pick a copy and share the load.
Incorrect: queuing for a full minute wrecks user experience — not a realistic fix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给同一个 key 加不同后缀创建的多份拷贝，分散到不同节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A suffixed copy duplicates a key under different suffixes so copies can live on different nodes.

q: 把 hot read 副本方案的流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the hot-read replica flow in the right order:
steps: 读请求随机选择一个带后缀的副本 key
监控发现 product:iphone 成为 hot key
为该 key 创建 product:iphone#1/#2/#3 等副本
一致性哈希把这些副本分散到不同节点
写入该 key 时更新所有副本并接受短暂不一致
why: 先识别热点，再复制该 key 并用一致性哈希分散到不同节点；写入换来读吞吐。
why_en: The flow detects the hot key, replicates it with suffixed copies spread by hashing, and trades extra write work for read throughput.
tradeoff: 识别与复制在先 vs 写入一致性代价在后

q: “整节点 read replica”和“只复制 hot key”的关键差异是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between a full-node read replica and copying only the hot key?
options: read replica 这种方案只能用来缓解写热点问题
两种方案在复制粒度上完全相同，没有任何区别
热点 key 的副本没法被读请求访问到
整节点复制整个 shard，热点副本只复制单个 key
options_en: Read replicas can only be used to relieve hot writes.
The two approaches replicate at exactly the same granularity, no difference at all.
Copies of a hot key cannot be reached by read requests.
A full replica copies the whole shard; a hot-key copy replicates just one key.
tradeoff: 精准但需生命周期管理 vs 简单但开销大
why: 整节点副本能分摊读但存储和复制开销大；hot key 副本只处理真正热点，需要监控和 promote/demote。
why_en: Full-node replicas spread reads but cost more storage and replication bandwidth, while hot-key copies target only the real hotspot and need monitoring plus promote/demote.
optionExplanations: 错：read replica 主要缓解读热点，不是写热点手段。
错：两者复制粒度完全不同，不是同一回事。
错：hot key 副本就是为了被读，分摊读流量正是它的价值。
对：复制范围不同，精准度和运维成本此消彼长。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: read replicas mainly relieve hot reads, not hot writes.
Incorrect: the two differ in copy granularity — they are not the same.
Incorrect: hot-key copies exist to be read; spreading reads is their whole point.
Correct: the copy scope differs, trading precision against lifecycle overhead.
scenario: 热点只集中在一个 key 上，但它所在的 shard 还存着几百万个冷 key。
scenario_en: The hotspot is a single key, but the shard holding it also stores millions of cold keys.

scenario: 某个 counter 每秒收到 10k 次增量写入，业务只关心短时间后最终值大致正确，不要求每次写立刻可见。
scenario_en: A counter receives 10k increment writes per second, and the business only needs the value to be roughly correct shortly afterward, not instantly visible after every write.
q: 哪种方案最先值得考虑？
q_en: Which mitigation should you consider first?
options: 给这个 counter 加更多读副本来分摊访问压力
写批处理：50-100ms 内合并成一次写
把所有写入都改成同步复制到全部副本节点
禁用缓存，让写请求直接打到数据库
options_en: Add more read replicas for the counter to spread the load.
Write batching: merge the updates into one write every 50-100ms.
Switch every write to synchronous replication across all replica nodes.
Disable the cache and send writes straight to the database.
tradeoff: 写吞吐提升 vs 写可见性延迟
why: 写批处理把短窗口内的多个更新合并成一次写，显著降压；代价是写可见性延后和失败恢复的复杂度。
why_en: Write batching merges many updates in a short window into one write, cutting pressure at the cost of delayed visibility and recovery complexity.
whenOtherWins: 若每次写必须立刻可见或严格排序，批处理窗口可能不可接受；读热点更适合用复制。
optionExplanations: 错：读副本只帮读，不减少这个 counter 收到的写次数。
对：合并更新次数，直接降低单 key 的写压力。
错：同步复制只会让每次写更慢，加重而不是缓解压力。
错：禁用缓存不是缓解方案，是放弃整个系统。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: read replicas only help reads; they don't reduce writes to this counter.
Correct: merging updates directly cuts the write count hitting this key.
Incorrect: synchronous replication makes every write slower, worsening the pressure.
Incorrect: disabling the cache isn't a mitigation — it abandons the system.

scenario: 一个 hot counter 写入太多，单 key 所在节点扛不住；该操作可分解和重组，例如总数可以由多个部分相加。
scenario_en: A hot counter receives too many writes for the node owning that single key, and the operation can be split and recombined, like summing partial counts.
q: 应该如何分散写负载？
q_en: How should you spread the write load?
options: 让所有请求都发到同一个节点，保持实现简单
给这个 key 加更多读副本，但所有写入仍然只打主 key
把 key 拆成多个子 key 写，读时聚合求和
每次写入前都对整个集群做一次全量扫描
options_en: Send every request to the same node to keep things simple.
Add more read replicas but still write only the primary key.
Split the key into subkeys for writes and sum them on read.
Do a full cluster scan before every write.
tradeoff: 写吞吐分散 vs 读需要聚合多个 shard
why: key sharding 用 views:video123:1..10 等子 key 分散写入，读总数时再 sum；用更慢的读换写吞吐。
why_en: Key sharding spreads writes across subkeys like views:video123:1..10 and sums them on read, trading slower reads for write throughput.
whenOtherWins: 若操作不能拆分重组，或读远多于写且延迟敏感，简单 key sharding 可能不合适。
optionExplanations: 错：单节点没有分散任何东西，热点依旧存在。
错：读副本不解决写入仍集中在同一个 key 的问题。
对：写随机分散到子 key，读时聚合还原总值。
错：每次写全量扫描是 O(n)，完全背离降压目标。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: a single node spreads nothing — the hotspot remains.
Incorrect: read replicas don't fix writes still landing on the same key.
Correct: writes fan out to subkeys and reads sum them back into a total.
Incorrect: scanning the whole cluster per write is O(n), the opposite of relief.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个热点 key 拆成多个子 key 分散写入，读时再聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key sharding splits one hot key into multiple subkeys to spread writes, aggregating them again on read.

q: 补全 hot write key sharding 的取舍：
q_en: Fill in the tradeoff for hot-write key sharding:
text: key sharding 把写压力从一个 key 分散到多个 {{sub-keys}}；读总值时需要 {{aggregate}} 多个 shard，因此牺牲读延迟换写吞吐。
why: 它适合可加和的 counter、metrics 等场景。子 key 太少无法分散，太多会让读聚合变慢。
why_en: Hot-write key sharding trades write scalability for more expensive aggregate reads.
tradeoff: 写吞吐提升 vs 读时聚合成本

q: 写批处理的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of write batching?
options: 用了批处理之后一致性哈希路由就没法再用了
批处理之后所有读请求都会自动变成强一致读
批处理会让实际写入次数多出一个数量级
窗口内更新暂不可见，处理器崩了要能重放
options_en: Once batching is in place, consistent-hashing routing can no longer be used.
After batching, every read automatically becomes strongly consistent.
Batching increases the actual number of writes by an order of magnitude.
Updates in the window are briefly invisible, and a crashed processor must be able to replay.
why: 批处理降压的代价是延迟写可见性，还要处理缓冲期失败；适合最终一致的计数器，不适合强实时写入。
why_en: Batching's cost is delayed write visibility plus needing recovery for buffer failures, so it suits eventually-consistent counters, not real-time writes.
optionExplanations: 错：批处理是写路径优化，跟路由算法无关。
错：批处理换来的是最终一致，不是强一致。
错：批处理是合并写入，次数应该下降而不是上升。
对：可见性延后和失败恢复正是批处理的两大风险。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: batching is a write-path optimization, unrelated to the routing algorithm.
Incorrect: batching yields eventual consistency, not strong consistency.
Incorrect: batching merges writes, so the count should drop, not rise.
Correct: delayed visibility and recovery-on-failure are the two real risks of batching.
scenario: 用 50-100ms 窗口合并计数器写入，批处理进程可能崩溃，看板最终不能少数。
scenario_en: You merge counter writes in a 50-100ms window, the batch processor can crash, and the dashboard still has to end up correct.

q: hot key 副本方案如果用在读写都很热的 key 上，可能会怎样？
q_en: What can happen if hot-key replicas are used for a key that is hot for both reads and writes?
options: 所有跟一致性相关的问题都会自动消失
写入必须更新更多份副本，反而放大了写压力和同步复杂度
读请求就没法再随机选择副本了
这个 key 的 TTL 设置会被强制禁止
options_en: All consistency-related problems disappear automatically.
Writes must update more copies, amplifying write pressure and sync complexity.
Reads can no longer randomly pick a copy.
TTL becomes forbidden for this key.
why: 读副本越多，写入要维护的一致性面越大；读多写少才是副本方案的舒适区。
why_en: More read copies mean more surface to keep consistent on every write, so replication is comfortable only when reads dominate writes.
optionExplanations: 错：多副本只解决读热点，写热点问题依然存在甚至加重。
对：每多一个副本，写入就多一次要同步的目标。
错：这个方案本身不影响读随机选择副本的能力。
错：TTL 是独立的过期机制，不受副本数量影响。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: more copies only helps hot reads; the hot-write problem remains or worsens.
Correct: every extra copy is one more target a write must keep in sync.
Incorrect: this approach doesn't affect randomized read selection.
Incorrect: TTL is an independent expiry mechanism, unaffected by replica count.
scenario: 某直播间计数 key 同时有 100k read/s 和 10k write/s，已经给它建了 10 份副本。
scenario_en: A live-room counter key takes 100k reads and 10k writes per second, and you already gave it ten replicas.

q: 文章提到哪些降低分布式缓存延迟的手段？（多选）
q_en: Which techniques reduce latency in a distributed cache? (multi-select)
options: 请求批处理减少网络往返
一致性哈希避免每次查中央路由
连接池复用长连接
每次请求都新建 TCP 连接
options_en: Request batching reduces network round trips.
Consistent hashing avoids querying a central router every time.
Connection pooling reuses long-lived connections.
Opening a new TCP connection on every request.
why: 分布式后延迟不只来自内存结构，还来自网络往返和连接建立；批处理、本地路由、连接池分别削减这些开销。
why_en: Once distributed, latency also comes from network round trips and connection setup, and batching, local routing, and pooling each cut a different piece of that overhead.
optionExplanations: 对：合并请求次数，直接省网络往返。
对：客户端本地算路由，省掉查中央路由的一跳。
对：复用已建立连接，省重复握手开销。
错：每次新建连接正是要避免的尾延迟来源。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: merging requests directly saves round trips.
Correct: local client-side routing skips the hop to a central router.
Correct: reusing connections avoids repeated handshake overhead.
Incorrect: opening a fresh connection every time is exactly the tail-latency source to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接的传输层协议，建立连接需要握手，有额外延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol whose handshake adds setup latency.

scenario: 缓存从单机变成 50 节点集群后，p99 get 从 1ms 涨到 12ms，超了 10ms 预算。
scenario_en: After moving from one box to a 50-node cluster, p99 get latency went from 1ms to 12ms, breaking the 10ms budget.

scenario: 客户端对缓存发起高频请求，如果每次都重新建 TCP/TLS 连接，p95/p99 延迟会被握手拖高。
scenario_en: The client sends high-frequency cache requests; if every request opens a new TCP/TLS connection, p95 and p99 latency are inflated by handshakes.
q: 应采用什么优化？
q_en: Which optimization should you use?
options: 把所有请求写到磁盘
每请求新建连接以保持干净
连接池 / 持久连接
禁用客户端 SDK
options_en: Write every request to disk.
Open a new connection per request to keep things clean.
Connection pooling / persistent connections.
Disable the client SDK.
tradeoff: 连接复用降尾延迟 vs 短连接的简单心智模型
why: 连接池复用已建立连接，避免重复握手和慢启动；缓存本身很快，连接管理常是尾延迟来源。
why_en: Connection pooling reuses established connections to skip repeated handshakes and slow-start, since connection setup is often the real source of tail latency.
whenOtherWins: 极低频的管理请求用简单短连接没问题；高频数据路径才需要复用连接。
optionExplanations: 错：写磁盘是持久化话题，跟连接管理无关。
错：每请求新建连接恰恰是尾延迟的来源。
对：复用连接省掉握手，直接压低 p95/p99。
错：禁用 SDK 无法发起请求，不是优化手段。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: writing to disk is a durability topic, unrelated to connection management.
Incorrect: opening a new connection per request is exactly the tail-latency source.
Correct: reusing connections skips handshakes and directly lowers p95/p99.
Incorrect: disabling the SDK means no requests can be made — not an optimization.

q: 为什么一致性哈希也算延迟优化？
q_en: Why does consistent hashing also count as a latency optimization?
options: 它把所有 key 都路由到了同一个节点上
它把内存里的哈希查找变成了 O(log n) 复杂度
它会在传输过程中自动压缩 value 的内容
客户端可以直接算出目标节点，省掉查询中央路由服务的一次网络往返
options_en: It routes every key to the same single node.
It turns the in-memory hash lookup into O(log n) complexity.
It automatically compresses value contents during transfer.
The client computes the target node directly, skipping a round trip to a central router.
why: 如果每次请求都先问路由服务，缓存的低延迟优势会被额外一跳吃掉；一致性哈希让路由变成本地计算。
why_en: If every request first asked a routing service, the cache's low-latency edge would be eaten by that extra hop, so consistent hashing turns routing into a local computation.
optionExplanations: 错：正相反，它的目的是把 key 分散到多个节点。
错：哈希查找本身仍是 O(1)，不是 O(log n)。
错：一致性哈希管路由，跟 value 压缩无关。
对：本地算路由，省掉那一次网络往返。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: it does the opposite — it spreads keys across many nodes.
Incorrect: hash lookup itself stays O(1), not O(log n).
Incorrect: consistent hashing governs routing, unrelated to value compression.
Correct: routing is computed locally, saving that network round trip.
scenario: 客户端每次读缓存前都要先问一次中央路由服务，这一跳吃掉了 10ms 预算的一半。
scenario_en: Clients query a central routing service before every cache read, and that hop eats half of the 10ms budget.

scenario: 面试官没有明确要求某种淘汰策略，只说容量有限、访问模式普通，没有特别的热点规律。
scenario_en: The interviewer does not require a specific eviction policy; capacity is limited, the workload is ordinary, and there is no special hot-key pattern.
q: 默认最稳妥的淘汰策略是什么？
q_en: What is the safest default eviction policy?
options: FIFO（先进先出），完全按插入顺序淘汰
随机挑一个 key 直接淘汰掉
LRU（最近最少使用）
永不淘汰，内存不够时直接报错拒绝写入
options_en: FIFO (first in, first out), evicting strictly by insertion order.
Randomly pick a key to evict.
LRU (least recently used).
Never evict, and reject writes once memory runs low.
tradeoff: 贴合常见访问模式 vs 特殊热点场景的专用策略
why: LRU 假设最近用过的还会再用，适配大多数工作负载，且可用哈希表+链表做到 O(1) 淘汰。
why_en: LRU assumes recently used data will be used again, fitting most workloads while still evicting in O(1) via a hash table and linked list.
whenOtherWins: 若有一批长期稳定的热门 key，LFU 通常更合适；需要强制刷新时再叠加 TTL。
optionExplanations: 错：FIFO 忽略使用频率，可能删掉仍然很热的数据。
错：随机淘汰没有任何访问模式感知，容易删有用数据。
对：安全默认，匹配“最近用过还会再用”的大多数场景。
错：永不淘汰会让内存无限增长，最终 OOM。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: FIFO ignores usage frequency and can evict data that's still hot.
Incorrect: random eviction has no access-pattern awareness and can delete useful data.
Correct: the safe default that matches 'recently used, likely used again' for most workloads.
Incorrect: never evicting lets memory grow unbounded until the process runs out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最少使用频率淘汰策略，优先删除被访问次数最少的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU evicts the entry that has been accessed the fewest times.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按插入顺序淘汰，不考虑是否仍被频繁访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO evicts by insertion order regardless of how often an entry is still being used.

q: 文章如何区分 partitioning 和 sharding？
q_en: How should you distinguish partitioning from sharding in this cache discussion?
options: 这两个词在含义上完全相反，不能互换
两者常被混用，sharding 特指跨节点拆分
sharding 这个词只能用来描述单机内存里的拆分
partitioning 这个词只能用在文件系统的语境里
options_en: The two terms mean opposite things and cannot be interchanged.
They're often used interchangeably; sharding specifically means splitting across nodes.
Sharding can only describe splitting inside a single machine's memory.
Partitioning can only apply in a file-system context.
tradeoff: 技术定义的范围 vs 分布式语境下的实际用法
why: 技术上 partitioning 可以发生在单系统内，sharding 特指跨节点；但分布式语境下两个词常被混用。
why_en: Technically partitioning can happen within one system while sharding specifically means splitting across nodes, though in distributed contexts the two words are often used interchangeably.
optionExplanations: 错：二者是包含/特化关系，不是对立关系。
对：范围包含关系，加上现实中混用的现象都说对了。
错：sharding 恰恰强调跨机器，不是单机内存概念。
错：partitioning 是通用概念，不限定文件系统场景。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: the two are a general/specific pair, not opposites.
Correct: it captures both the containment relationship and the real-world interchangeable usage.
Incorrect: sharding specifically emphasizes across-machine splitting, not single-machine memory.
Incorrect: partitioning is a general concept, not limited to file systems.
scenario: 你要同时描述“单节点内部拆数据”和“跨 50 台机器拆数据”，用词不能让面试官听混。
scenario_en: You have to describe both splitting data inside one node and splitting it across 50 machines, and the wording must not confuse the interviewer.

q: 把“从单机缓存到可扩展集群”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain from single-node cache to scalable cluster in the right order:
steps: 用一致性哈希把 key 分布到节点，节点变化时少搬数据
需求：1TB 数据和 100k RPS，单机无法承载
每个节点内部仍用 hash table + LRU list
容量估算显示约 50 个节点由存储驱动
对每个 shard 做异步复制以提高可用性
why: 先由容量确认必须分片，再选择一致性哈希路由，并用复制提升可用性；单节点内部的数据结构仍然是缓存行为的基础。
why_en: The scalable-cache chain starts with capacity forcing sharding, adds consistent-hash routing, layers on async replication for availability, while each node still runs a hash table plus LRU list internally.
tradeoff: 先分片保证水平扩展 vs 先复制保证可用性

q: 把“处理 hot read key”的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for handling a hot-read key in the right order:
steps: 接受写入时要更新所有副本且可能短暂不一致
需求：单个 key 的读流量压垮所在 shard
用监控识别并提升 hot key
创建多个后缀副本并分散到不同节点
读请求随机选择副本分摊负载
why: 读热点的目标是分散读，不是搬动全库；代价集中在副本管理和写入一致性上。
why_en: The hot-read chain aims to spread reads rather than move the whole dataset, concentrating its cost in replica management and write consistency.
tradeoff: 读分摊收益 vs 副本同步代价

q: 生产级 LRU 伪代码之外还必须考虑什么？
q_en: Beyond LRU pseudocode, what must a production implementation still handle?
options: 删除所有过期策略
只考虑语法是否像 Python
线程安全、错误处理、监控、性能优化
禁止并发访问
options_en: Removing all expiry policies.
Only whether the syntax looks like Python.
Thread safety, error handling, monitoring, and performance tuning.
Forbidding concurrent access.
why: 文章代码只讲核心概念；真实缓存节点还要处理并发、内存压力、监控、错误和尾延迟。
why_en: The article's pseudocode only illustrates the core idea; a production cache node still needs concurrency control, monitoring, error handling, and tail-latency work.
optionExplanations: 错：生产实现要保留过期策略，不是删掉它。
错：语法是否像 Python 只是表达方式，不是工程问题。
对：这些正是伪代码故意省略、留给生产实现的部分。
错：禁止并发违背了缓存要支撑高并发的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: production still keeps expiry policies rather than removing them.
Incorrect: syntax style is just presentation, not an engineering concern.
Correct: these are exactly what the pseudocode deliberately leaves for production.
Incorrect: forbidding concurrency defeats the cache's whole purpose of serving high concurrency.
scenario: 白板上的 LRU 伪代码要上线成 50 节点集群的一部分，每节点多线程扛 20k RPS。
scenario_en: The whiteboard LRU pseudocode now has to ship inside a 50-node cluster where each node serves 20k requests per second across threads.

q: 文章最终设计可能包含哪些要点？（多选）
q_en: Which points belong in the final distributed-cache design? (multi-select)
options: 每个节点有 hash table 存 key-value
每个节点有 linked list 支撑 LRU
一致性哈希做分片路由
复杂 SQL 引擎处理 ad-hoc query
options_en: Each node has a hash table storing key-value pairs.
Each node has a linked list backing LRU.
Consistent hashing does shard routing.
A complex SQL engine handles ad-hoc queries.
why: 最终设计把单节点结构 hash table+LRU list 跟分布式机制分片、复制、热点处理组合起来；SQL 不是缓存主线。
why_en: The final design combines the per-node hash table and LRU list with distributed sharding, replication, and hot-key handling — SQL querying stays out of scope.
optionExplanations: 对：单节点存取的基本数据结构。
对：单节点内维护访问顺序的数据结构。
对：跨节点分片路由的机制。
错：复杂查询是数据库范畴，明确 below the line。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the basic per-node storage structure.
Correct: the per-node structure that tracks access order.
Correct: the cross-node sharding mechanism.
Incorrect: complex querying is a database concern, explicitly out of scope.
scenario: 面试收尾要复述这套 1TB/100k RPS 缓存的最终架构；源数据仍留在后端数据库。
scenario_en: To wrap up you recap the final architecture of this 1TB, 100k-RPS cache, with the backend database still the system of record.

scenario: 这是缓存而不是系统记录，源数据通常还能从后端数据库重新加载；用户可接受短暂 stale 数据。
scenario_en: This is a cache, not the system of record; source data can usually be reloaded from the backend database, and users can tolerate brief staleness.
q: 这会如何影响一致性选择？
q_en: How does that affect the consistency choice?
options: 完全不允许任何副本存在，全集群只留一份数据
必须做到线性一致，每次读都要拿到最新写入的那个值
所有写入都必须走两阶段提交并等全部副本确认
优先可用性和性能，接受最终一致
options_en: No replicas at all are allowed; the cluster keeps a single copy of the data.
It must be linearizable, so every read returns the very latest write.
Every write must go through two-phase commit and wait for all replicas.
Prioritize availability and performance, accepting eventual consistency.
tradeoff: 可用性与延迟 vs 强一致保证
why: 缓存的价值是快和可用，短暂 stale 通常比缓存不可用更能接受；文章也明确把强一致放在范围外。
why_en: A cache's value is speed and availability, so brief staleness is usually more acceptable than the cache being unavailable, and strong consistency is explicitly out of scope.
whenOtherWins: 若缓存要承载库存扣减或余额这类唯一真相，就不能用这种弱一致假设。
optionExplanations: 错：不允许副本会直接牺牲高可用这个核心需求。
错：线性一致要求同步协调，牺牲的正是这里要保的可用性。
错：两阶段提交是跨系统事务方案，不是缓存该有的开销。
对：源数据可重建，用户能接受短暂 stale，正好换可用性。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: disallowing replicas directly sacrifices the core high-availability requirement.
Incorrect: linearizability needs synchronous coordination, sacrificing exactly the availability being prioritized here.
Incorrect: two-phase commit is a cross-system transaction tool, not overhead a cache should carry.
Correct: the source data is recoverable and users tolerate brief staleness, so it's a fair trade for availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的一致性模型，所有操作看起来像是按一个全局顺序原子发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability is the strongest consistency model, making all operations appear to happen atomically in one global order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨节点事务协议，先都准备好再统一提交，保证要么全部成功要么全部回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a cross-node transaction protocol that first prepares all participants, then commits them together.

q: hot key 方案为什么需要监控和 promote/demote 机制？
q_en: Why does a hot-key strategy need monitoring plus promote and demote mechanics?
options: 因为 LRU 机制没办法删除一个普通的 key
热点会消退，副本不回收就白烧资源
因为一致性哈希没办法处理新节点的加入
因为集群里所有的 key 其实永远都是热点
options_en: Because LRU cannot delete a normal key.
Hotspots fade, and copies that are never reclaimed just burn resources.
Because consistent hashing cannot handle new nodes joining.
Because every key in the cluster is always hot.
why: 热点通常由事件驱动，可能很快消退；复制或提升后必须能降级回普通路径，否则成本和一致性负担会累积。
why_en: Hotspots are often event-driven and can fade quickly, so promoted copies must be demotable back to the normal path or cost and consistency burden keep accumulating.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Metrics[Key metrics] --> Detect[Detect hot key]
Detect --> Promote[Promote replicas]
Promote --> Observe[Watch load]
Observe --> Demote[Demote when cool]
optionExplanations: 错：LRU 淘汰和 hot key 生命周期管理是两回事。
对：热点会退潮，不回收副本就是白白多付成本。
错：一致性哈希本身能处理新节点加入，与此无关。
错：热点是少数 key 的现象，不是全部 key 的常态。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: LRU eviction and hot-key lifecycle management are separate concerns.
Correct: hotspots fade, and unreclaimed copies simply keep costing you for nothing.
Incorrect: consistent hashing already handles new nodes joining; that's unrelated here.
Incorrect: hotspots affect a handful of keys, not the steady state of every key.
scenario: 世界杯期间某热点 key 被复制成 10 份，赛后流量回落，副本还在占内存和写带宽。
scenario_en: A World Cup hot key was replicated ten ways; after the match the traffic drops but those copies still burn memory and write bandwidth.

q: 把这题讲清楚时，哪些“不要过度设计”的判断是正确的？（多选）
q_en: When explaining this design, which 'do not over-design' judgments are correct? (multi-select)
options: API 和实体很简单，应快速通过
先做单机可工作的 TTL/LRU，再加分布式扩展
复杂查询和事务不用塞进缓存设计
必须从一开始就设计为强一致数据库
options_en: The API and entities are simple, so move through them quickly.
Build a working single-node TTL/LRU cache first, then add distributed scaling.
Complex querying and transactions don't belong in a cache design.
It must be designed as a strongly consistent database from the start.
why: 文章强调这题要展示灵活度：低层实现和高层扩展都要有，但别把范围外的数据库能力硬塞进来。
why_en: This question rewards flexibility — cover both the low-level implementation and the high-level scaling, without dragging in out-of-scope database features.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client SDK] -->|consistent hash route| N1[Cache Node A]
Client --> N2[Cache Node B]
Client --> N3[Cache Node C]
N1 --> R1[Async Replica]
N2 --> R2[Async Replica]
N3 --> R3[Async Replica]
Hot[Hot Key Copies] --> N1
Hot --> N2
Hot --> N3
optionExplanations: 对：这两部分本来就轻，面试该把时间留给深挖。
对：先建可工作的地基，再叠加分布式复杂度是推荐顺序。
对：复杂查询和事务明确 below the line。
错：强一致数据库违背了缓存本身接受 eventual consistency 的前提。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: these two parts are inherently light, so save interview time for the deep dives.
Correct: build a working foundation first, then layer on distributed complexity — the recommended order.
Correct: complex querying and transactions are explicitly out of scope.
Incorrect: a strongly consistent database contradicts the cache's own eventual-consistency premise.
scenario: 45 分钟面试要从单机 TTL/LRU 一路讲到分布式扩展，时间不够，必须砍掉旁支。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to go from single-node TTL/LRU all the way to distributed scaling, so side branches have to be cut.

scenario: LRU 缓存每次 get 命中都要把链表中间的那个 node 摘出来放到表头，单节点扛 20k RPS，这一步必须是 O(1)，不能沿链表扫。
scenario_en: LRU caches must unlink a node from the middle of the list and move it to the front on every hit; at 20k requests per second on a single host this step has to be O(1), with no scanning.
q: 访问顺序链表为什么必须用双向链表？
q_en: Why does the access-order list have to be a doubly-linked list?
options: 单链表就够：把要移动的 node 打上删除标记，等到淘汰时再一并跳过
哈希表本来就能直接返回某个 node 的前驱，所以单链表也能 O(1) 摘除
node 自带 prev 指针，摘除中间节点不用从头找前驱
换成按访问时间排序的数组，插入和删除元素同样是常数开销
options_en: A singly-linked list is enough: tombstone the node you want to move and skip it later at eviction time.
The hash table can hand you a node's predecessor directly, so a singly-linked list still unlinks in O(1).
Each node carries a prev pointer, so unlinking a middle node needs no walk from the head.
Switch to an array sorted by access time — inserts and deletes there are constant-cost too.
tradeoff: 每个 node 多一个指针的内存 vs 摘除中间节点的时间复杂度
why: 摘除一个节点必须改它前驱的 next；单链表要从头遍历才能找到前驱，退化成 O(n)。代价是每个 entry 多存一个 prev 指针的内存。
why_en: Unlinking a node means rewriting its predecessor's next pointer, and a singly-linked list has to walk from the head to find that predecessor, which degrades to O(n). The cost is one extra pointer of memory per entry.
whenOtherWins: 如果链表只在尾部淘汰、从不移动中间节点（例如 FIFO 而非 LRU），单链表就够用，可以省下 prev 指针。
optionExplanations: 错：标记删除会让链表越积越长，遍历和内存都被墓碑拖垮。
错：哈希表存的是 key → node，它不知道谁排在这个 node 前面。
对：prev 指针让"改前驱的 next"变成一次指针赋值。
错：数组中间插删要整体搬移元素，是 O(n) 不是常数。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: tombstones let the list grow without bound, dragging down both traversal and memory.
Incorrect: the hash table maps key to node; it has no idea which node sits in front of it.
Correct: the prev pointer turns "rewrite the predecessor's next" into a single pointer assignment.
Incorrect: inserting or deleting in the middle of an array shifts elements, which is O(n), not constant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个节点同时存前驱和后继指针的链表，可在 O(1) 内摘除任意已知节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A doubly-linked list stores both a previous and a next pointer in every node, so any known node can be unlinked in constant time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略：内存满时先丢掉最久没被访问的那个 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU means least recently used: when memory fills up, the key that has gone longest without access is evicted first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量单节点吞吐的单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPS stands for requests per second, the unit used to measure a single node's throughput.

scenario: 集群用主从异步复制：写只等主节点确认，再异步推给副本。某个分片的主节点整机宕机，客户端仍在往这个分片写。
scenario_en: The cluster uses primary-replica asynchronous replication: a write is acknowledged by the primary and pushed to replicas afterwards. One shard's primary dies outright while clients keep writing to that shard.
q: 这个分片接下来会走完怎样的恢复过程？
q_en: What recovery sequence does that shard go through next?
options: 副本会自动顶上成为新主，整个过程零中断，客户端完全无感知
需要先选出一个副本 promote 成新主，切换窗口内该分片写不可用
一致性哈希会把这个分片的写永久重路由到相邻分片的主节点上
集群会停下来等原机器修复重启，期间这个分片降级为只读继续对外提供服务
options_en: A replica takes over automatically with zero interruption, and clients notice nothing at all.
A replica has to be elected and promoted to primary first, and writes to that shard fail during the switchover window.
Consistent hashing permanently reroutes this shard's writes to the neighbouring shard's primary.
The cluster halts and waits for the original machine to be repaired and rebooted, serving the shard read-only to clients meanwhile.
why: 异步复制只有主能收写，主一挂就必须先选出并 promote 一个副本；这段 failover 窗口该分片写不可用，且主已确认但还没推给副本的写会永久丢失。
why_en: With asynchronous replication only the primary accepts writes, so when it dies a replica must be elected and promoted first; during that failover window the shard cannot take writes, and anything the primary acknowledged but had not yet shipped is lost for good.
optionExplanations: 错：promote 需要检测故障、选主、更新路由，中间必然有一段写失败。
对：这正是异步复制换来的性能所对应的运维代价。
错：一致性哈希决定 key 落在哪个分片，不负责主副本的角色切换。
错：主已经没了，只读也拿不到最新写，等修机器的停机时间不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: promotion needs failure detection, election and routing updates, so some writes are guaranteed to fail in between.
Correct: this is the operational price paid for the performance async replication buys.
Incorrect: consistent hashing decides which shard a key lands on; it does not switch primary roles.
Incorrect: the primary is gone, read-only cannot serve the latest writes, and waiting for a repair is unacceptable downtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点失效后把流量切到接替者的过程，包含故障检测、选主和路由更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover is the process of shifting traffic to a stand-in after the primary fails, covering detection, election and routing updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个只读副本改成可接受写入的新主节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To promote is to turn a read-only replica into the new primary that accepts writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把节点和 key 排在一个哈希环上，增删节点时只有一段 key 需要重新映射。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places nodes and keys on a hash ring so that adding or removing a node remaps only one slice of keys.

scenario: 监控显示少数几个 key 吃掉全集群一大半读流量，而且请求集中在某几个地区；你不想为它们把 50 个节点全部升级硬件。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows a handful of keys absorbing most of the cluster's read traffic, concentrated in a few geographic regions, and you do not want to upgrade the hardware of all 50 nodes just for them.
q: 该用哪种缓存层结构承接这批热 key？
q_en: Which cache-layer structure should absorb those hot keys?
options: 把集群里全部 50 个节点的 CPU、内存和网卡都升级一档
给这批 key 设置很短的 TTL，让它们尽快过期离开集群
把这批 key 直接从缓存里删掉，所有读请求都回源到后端数据库
建一个独立的 hot-key 缓存层，用更强硬件、按地域就近部署
options_en: Upgrade the CPU, memory and network capacity of all 50 nodes in the cluster.
Give those keys a very short TTL so they expire out of the cluster quickly.
Drop those keys from the cache entirely and send every read back to the backing database.
Stand up a separate hot-key cache tier on beefier hardware, deployed close to users by region.
tradeoff: 把资源精准投在热点上 vs 多维护一套基础设施的运维与一致性成本
why: 热点只集中在少数 key 上，专用 tier 让你只为这几个 key 花更强硬件，还能就近部署压低跨地域延迟。代价是多一套基础设施，以及两层之间的一致性管理。
why_en: The heat sits on just a few keys, so a dedicated tier lets you spend beefier hardware only on those and place them near users to cut cross-region latency. The cost is a second piece of infrastructure plus keeping the two tiers consistent.
whenOtherWins: 如果热度分散在成千上万个 key 上而不是少数几个，专用 tier 无从挑选，整体扩容或加节点更实在。
optionExplanations: 错：为少数热点给全集群升级，成本随节点数线性上涨，不可持续。
错：缩短 TTL 只会让热 key 更频繁地被重建，读压力不降反升。
错：把最热的 key 移出缓存，正好把最大的流量打到数据库上。
对：资源精准投在热点上，还顺便拿到地理就近的收益。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: upgrading the whole cluster for a few hot keys scales cost linearly with node count and is unsustainable.
Incorrect: a shorter TTL just makes the hot key get rebuilt more often, raising read pressure rather than lowering it.
Incorrect: evicting the hottest keys sends exactly the largest traffic straight at the database.
Correct: resources land precisely on the hotspots, with geographic proximity as a bonus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 收到远超其他 key 的流量的那个 key，会把它所在分片打成瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key receives disproportionately more traffic than other keys and turns the shard holding it into a bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活时间：给 key 设的过期时长，到点后条目自动失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL stands for time to live, the lifetime set on a key after which the entry expires automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在主缓存之外单独部署的一层缓存，硬件规格和部署位置可以与主层不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tier here is a separately deployed cache layer whose hardware and placement can differ from the main layer.

scenario: 异步复制的分片里，一个副本因网络分区离线了 5 分钟；这期间主节点照常接受并确认写入，只是推不到这个副本。
scenario_en: In an asynchronously replicated shard, one replica goes offline for five minutes due to a network partition, while the primary keeps accepting and acknowledging writes it cannot ship to that replica.
q: 副本重新上线后必须先做什么才能承接读？
q_en: What has to happen before that replica can serve reads again?
options: 追踪它离线期间漏掉的那批更新并补齐，否则它会把旧值当成有效值返回
什么都不用做，直接开始服务读，落后的部分会被 TTL 自动抹平
把这个分片的主节点一起重启，让主和副本从空缓存重新开始积累
立刻把这个副本 promote 成新主，用它自己的状态覆盖主节点的状态
options_en: Track the updates it missed while offline and replay them, or it will hand back stale values as if they were fresh.
Nothing at all — it can start serving reads immediately, and TTL will smooth over whatever it is behind on.
Restart the shard's primary as well, so primary and replica both start over from an empty cache.
Promote the replica to primary right away and let its own state overwrite the primary's.
why: 异步复制不等副本确认，离线窗口内的写只存在于主节点上；不补齐这段缺口，副本恢复后每次命中都可能返回 stale 值。代价是要记录并重放这批更新。
why_en: Asynchronous replication never waits for replica acknowledgement, so writes made during the outage exist only on the primary; without replaying that gap the replica returns stale values on every hit. The cost is tracking and replaying those updates.
optionExplanations: 对：这正是异步复制在故障恢复上比同步复制复杂的地方。
错：TTL 只管过期，管不了"值还在但已经过时"这种情况。
错：清空整个分片会把命中率打到零，读流量全部压到数据库。
错：副本的状态比主更旧，拿它覆盖主等于主动丢掉 5 分钟的写。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: this is precisely where async replication is harder to recover than synchronous replication.
Incorrect: TTL only handles expiry, not the case where a value is still present but out of date.
Incorrect: wiping the whole shard drops the hit rate to zero and dumps all read traffic on the database.
Incorrect: the replica's state is older than the primary's, so overwriting means deliberately discarding five minutes of writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点确认写入后再把变更推给副本，写不等副本回应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In asynchronous replication the primary acknowledges a write first and ships the change to replicas afterwards, without waiting for them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 副本上还没收到最新写入，因而返回的旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stale data is an older value returned by a replica that has not yet received the latest write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点之间网络中断，彼此可达性丢失但各自仍在运行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is a loss of connectivity between nodes that are each still running on their own.

scenario: 50 节点这个数字建立在两个假设上：单机 20k RPS、32GB 内存里约 24GB 可用于缓存数据。而你们的 value 平均 8KB，访问模式也和假设不同。
scenario_en: The 50-node figure rests on two assumptions: 20k requests per second per host, and about 24GB of a 32GB machine usable for cache data. Your values average 8KB and your access pattern differs from the assumption.
q: 这两个假设数字应该怎么用？
q_en: How should those two assumed numbers be used?
options: 当成公认的行业标准值直接采用并写进容量规划文档，它们与实例规格和访问模式都没有关系
按 24GB 反推，把每个 value 都压缩到更小以匹配这个内存假设
把节点数乘以 2 当作安全系数，这样就不必再做任何测量了
当成示例量级，上线前用真实 workload benchmark 出自己的单机容量
options_en: Adopt them as accepted industry standards and write them into the capacity plan — they do not depend on instance spec or access pattern.
Work backwards from 24GB and compress every value smaller so it matches that memory assumption.
Multiply the node count by two as a safety factor, so no further measurement is needed.
Treat them as illustrative orders of magnitude, then benchmark your real workload for true per-host capacity.
tradeoff: 用现成假设快速给出数量级 vs 用真实 benchmark 得到可承诺的容量
why: 节点数 = 数据总量 ÷ 单机可用内存 = 1024GB ÷ 24GB ≈ 43，取 50。但 20k RPS 与 24GB 都是示例假设，真实值随实例类型、value 大小和访问模式变化，必须自己压测。
why_en: Node count equals total data divided by usable memory per host: 1024GB over 24GB is about 43, rounded up to 50. But both 20k RPS and 24GB are illustrative assumptions that shift with instance type, value size and access pattern, so you must benchmark your own.
whenOtherWins: 白板上时间只够给数量级时，直接套这类粗估反而合适——面试考的是推导链，不是精确容量。
optionExplanations: 错：单机能扛多少完全取决于实例规格和数据形状，没有通用常数。
错：假设是为了估算方便，不该反过来约束业务的数据形状。
错：乘以 2 只是把误差放大，方向对不对仍然没人知道。
对：粗估先定数量级，benchmark 再把它变成能对外承诺的容量。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: what one host can take depends entirely on instance spec and data shape; there is no universal constant.
Incorrect: the assumption exists to make estimation easy, not to constrain the shape of the business data.
Incorrect: doubling only scales the error up; nobody still knows whether the direction is right.
Correct: rough math fixes the order of magnitude, and benchmarking turns it into capacity you can commit to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用贴近真实的负载测量系统实际能承受的吞吐和容量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Benchmarking measures the throughput and capacity a system actually sustains under a realistic load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实流量的形状：读写比、请求速率、value 大小和访问分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A workload is the shape of real traffic: read-write mix, request rate, value size and access distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量吞吐的单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPS stands for requests per second, the unit of throughput.

scenario: 你按 1024GB ÷ 24GB 给出约 50 节点的粗估，面试官追问：还有哪些因素会推翻这个数字？（多选）
scenario_en: You produced the rough estimate of about 50 nodes from 1024GB divided by 24GB, and the interviewer asks which factors could overturn that number. (multi-select)
q: 哪些因素会改变这个集群规模估算？
q_en: Which factors would change this cluster-size estimate?
options: 实例类型：换更大内存的机型直接抬高单机可用容量
value 平均大小：value 越大，同样内存装下的 entry 越少
读写比与复制系数：每份数据存几副本会成倍放大总内存需求
预期增长率：按今天的数据量买机器，半年后又要重新扩容
客户端用什么编程语言写的
options_en: Instance type: a machine with more memory directly raises usable capacity per host.
Average value size: bigger values mean fewer entries fit in the same memory.
Read-write ratio and replication factor: how many copies you keep multiplies total memory demand.
Expected growth rate: sizing for today's data means re-scaling again in six months.
Which programming language the client is written in.
why: 50 节点来自"总数据量 ÷ 单机可用内存"这一个除法；任何改变分子或分母的因素都会平移结果，所以报数字时必须同时说清依赖的假设。
why_en: The 50-node figure comes from a single division — total data over usable memory per host — so anything that moves the numerator or denominator moves the answer, which is why you state your assumptions alongside the number.
optionExplanations: 对：它改的是除法的分母，节点数随之等比缩放。
对：它决定同样内存能装多少条目，影响真实可用容量。
对：复制系数是乘在总量上的，3 副本就是 3 倍内存。
对：容量规划要留 headroom，否则很快又触顶。
错：客户端语言影响 SDK 实现，不影响服务端要多少内存。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: it changes the denominator of the division, scaling node count proportionally.
Correct: it decides how many entries fit in the same memory, changing real usable capacity.
Correct: the replication factor multiplies the total, so three copies means three times the memory.
Correct: capacity planning needs headroom, or you hit the ceiling again almost immediately.
Incorrect: client language affects the SDK implementation, not how much memory the servers need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每份数据在集群里保存的副本数量，直接乘在总存储需求上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The replication factor is how many copies of each piece of data the cluster keeps, and it multiplies total storage demand directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 规划容量时预留的富余，用来吸收流量尖峰、节点故障和数据增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Headroom is the spare capacity reserved to absorb traffic spikes, node failures and data growth.

scenario: LRU 淘汰是从链表尾部摘下一个 node，同时还得把它从哈希表里删掉，而哈希表是 key → node 的单向映射。
scenario_en: LRU eviction unlinks a node from the tail of the list and must also delete it from the hash table, which maps key to node in one direction only.
q: 链表 node 里为什么除了 value 还要存 key？
q_en: Why does each list node store the key as well as the value?
options: 为了让哈希表能按 key 排序，从而支持前缀查询和范围扫描
没有 key 就没法反查哈希表条目，淘汰后会留下指向已删节点的映射
为了在 TTL 到期时用 key 重新计算这个 entry 的过期时间戳
为了让链表能按 key 的字典序维持有序，加快查找命中位置
options_en: So the hash table can be ordered by key, enabling prefix lookups and range scans.
Without the key you cannot look the entry back up in the hash table, leaving a mapping to a deleted node behind.
So an expired entry can have its expiry timestamp recomputed from the key when TTL fires.
So the list stays sorted in lexicographic key order, speeding up where a lookup lands.
why: 淘汰是从链表这一侧发起的，那里手上只有 node；node 自带 key 才能执行 delete data[lru.key]。漏掉这一步，哈希表就指向已删节点，下次 get 拿到脏引用。
why_en: Eviction starts from the list side, where all you hold is a node, so the node must carry its key to run delete data of that key. Skip it and the hash table points at a freed node, and the next get picks up a dangling reference.
optionExplanations: 错：哈希表本来就无序，LRU 也不需要按 key 排序。
对：两个结构存的是同一批 entry，删除必须两边同时发生。
错：过期时间戳在 set 时就算好存进 node，不需要重算。
错：链表维护的是访问顺序，不是 key 顺序，查找靠哈希表。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: a hash table is unordered by nature, and LRU has no need for key ordering.
Correct: both structures hold the same entries, so a delete has to happen on both sides at once.
Incorrect: the expiry timestamp is computed at set time and stored on the node; nothing needs recomputing.
Incorrect: the list maintains access order, not key order, and lookups go through the hash table.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 到值的映射结构，提供 O(1) 的查找与插入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash table maps keys to values and gives constant-time lookup and insertion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活时间：给 key 设的过期时长，到点后条目失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL stands for time to live, the lifetime set on a key after which the entry expires.

scenario: 面试官只说"设计一个像 Redis 的分布式缓存"，没有给数据量和 QPS；你打算先问清规模再写非功能需求。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says "design a distributed cache like Redis" without giving data volume or QPS, and you plan to pin down the scale before writing non-functional requirements.
q: 先确认规模主要是为了定下什么？
q_en: What does confirming the scale first actually pin down?
options: API 的路径命名与请求体字段格式，先把接口契约定死再往下设计
淘汰策略到底该选 LRU 还是 LFU，以及过期检查用什么频率
非功能需求的具体取值，它决定了要不要分片和复制
面试 45 分钟里各个环节的时间分配，避免在实体上花太久
options_en: The API paths and request body fields, locking the interface contract down before designing further.
Whether eviction should be LRU or LFU, and how often the expiry sweep runs.
The concrete values of the non-functional requirements, which decide whether you need sharding and replication.
How the 45 interview minutes are split across sections, so you do not overspend on entities.
why: 规模是 NFR 的输入：1TB 和 100k RPS 才逼出分片、复制和多节点路由；若只是单机几 GB，整个分布式部分都不必设计。代价是开场先花一两分钟问。
why_en: Scale is the input to the non-functional requirements: it takes 1TB and 100k requests per second to force sharding, replication and multi-node routing, whereas a few gigabytes on one box needs none of it. The cost is a minute or two of asking up front.
optionExplanations: 错：get/set/delete 三个接口跟规模无关，量级再大也是这三个。
错：淘汰策略由业务访问模式决定，也要问，但不是规模决定的。
对：数量级直接决定后半段有没有分布式内容可讲。
错：时间分配是你自己的策略，不需要向面试官确认规模才能定。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: get, set and delete are the same three endpoints no matter how large the deployment gets.
Incorrect: eviction policy follows the access pattern and is worth asking about, but scale does not decide it.
Correct: the order of magnitude decides whether there is any distributed content in the second half at all.
Incorrect: time allocation is your own tactic and does not require confirming scale with the interviewer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非功能需求：可用性、延迟、可扩展性这类对系统质量的要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NFR stands for non-functional requirement, covering qualities such as availability, latency and scalability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量系统请求吞吐的单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS stands for queries per second, the unit for a system's request throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最不经常使用淘汰策略：按访问次数而不是最近时间来淘汰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU stands for least frequently used, evicting by access count rather than by recency.

scenario: 热 key product:iphone 已被 promote 到独立的 hot-key 缓存层，读流量走那一层；但写路径没改，仍然只更新主缓存集群。
scenario_en: The hot key product:iphone has been promoted into a dedicated hot-key cache tier that now serves its reads, but the write path was never changed and still updates only the main cache cluster.
q: 闪购期间改价后，这条写路径会造成什么？
q_en: After a flash-sale price change, what does that write path cause?
options: hot tier 上的这个 key 会立刻失效，读请求全部穿透回后端数据库
一致性哈希会自动把这个 key 路由回主集群，两层不一致的问题自行消失
hot tier 继续用旧价格应答，而它承接的恰恰是流量最大的那批读
主集群会因为检测不到 hot tier 的确认而拒绝这次写入并报错
options_en: The key on the hot tier is invalidated immediately and every read falls through to the backing database.
Consistent hashing reroutes the key back to the main cluster automatically and the divergence resolves itself.
The hot tier keeps answering with the old price, and it is serving exactly the highest-volume reads.
The main cluster rejects the write with an error because it never sees an acknowledgement from the hot tier.
why: 同一个 key 在两层各存一份，promote 之后必须有机制把写同步到 hot tier 并决定何时 demote。漏掉同步的代价被流量放大：错的正是被读得最多的那个 key。
why_en: The same key now lives in two tiers, so once it is promoted something has to propagate writes into the hot tier and decide when to demote it. Missing that sync gets amplified by traffic: the stale value is on the most-read key you have.
optionExplanations: 错：主集群的写不会通知 hot tier，那一份不会自己失效。
错：一致性哈希只在主集群内部选分片，管不到独立的 hot tier。
对：这就是专用 tier 换来的性能背后要付的一致性管理成本。
错：写路径根本不知道 hot tier 存在，也就无从等待它确认。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: a write to the main cluster never notifies the hot tier, so that copy does not invalidate itself.
Incorrect: consistent hashing only picks shards inside the main cluster and has no reach into a separate tier.
Correct: this is the consistency-management cost behind the performance a dedicated tier buys.
Incorrect: the write path does not know the hot tier exists, so it cannot wait for an acknowledgement from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 提升到专用热点层，或在热度消退后把它降回主缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Promoting moves a key up into the dedicated hot tier, and demoting sends it back to the main cache once the heat fades.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门承接热点 key 的独立缓存层，硬件更强、可按地域部署。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot tier is a separate cache layer dedicated to hot keys, running on stronger hardware and deployable per region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把节点和 key 排在哈希环上决定归属，增删节点只重映射一小段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing arranges nodes and keys on a ring to decide ownership, remapping only a small slice when nodes change.

scenario: 热 key 被复制成 user:123#1 到 #4，分散在 4 个节点上分摊读；一次写要更新全部 4 份，而系统的非功能需求接受最终一致。
scenario_en: A hot key is copied as user:123#1 through #4 across four nodes to spread reads, a single write must update all four copies, and the system's non-functional requirements accept eventual consistency.
q: 接受最终一致让写路径省掉了什么？
q_en: What does accepting eventual consistency save on the write path?
options: 不必再监控哪些 key 是热点，副本可以一直保留在集群里不回收
不必用一致性哈希做路由，读请求打到任意节点都能拿到正确值
不必原子地更新 4 份副本，允许它们短暂不一致后再收敛
不必更新任何副本，读到旧值时由客户端自己回源重建这一份
options_en: You no longer need to monitor which keys are hot, and the copies can simply stay in the cluster forever.
You no longer need consistent hashing for routing, since any node can answer a read correctly.
You no longer need to update the four copies atomically; they may diverge briefly and converge afterwards.
You no longer need to update copies at all — clients that read a stale value rebuild it from the source.
why: 要让 4 份副本原子可见就得引入跨节点协调，复杂度和写延迟都跳一级；缓存允许短暂不一致，写只需逐份推送并等它们收敛。代价是同一时刻不同副本可能给出不同值。
why_en: Making four copies atomically visible would need cross-node coordination, which jumps both complexity and write latency; since a cache tolerates brief divergence, writes just push to each copy and let them converge. The cost is that different copies may disagree at the same instant.
optionExplanations: 错：热度会消退，副本不回收就在白烧内存和写带宽。
错：带后缀的副本正是靠一致性哈希才被分散到不同节点的。
对：省掉的是跨节点原子提交这一整套协调机制。
错：写不推副本的话，读随机命中哪份就返回哪份的旧值，永远不收敛。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: heat fades, and copies that are never reclaimed just burn memory and replication bandwidth.
Incorrect: it is consistent hashing that spreads the suffixed copies across different nodes in the first place.
Correct: what you skip is the whole cross-node atomic-commit coordination.
Incorrect: if writes never reach the copies, reads return whichever stale copy they land on and never converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许副本短暂不一致，只要停止写入后它们最终收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows replicas to diverge briefly as long as they converge on the same value once writes stop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多份数据要么一起对外可见，要么都不可见，中间态不暴露。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic update makes several copies visible together or not at all, never exposing an intermediate state.

scenario: key sharding 把热写 key 拆成 views:video123:1 到 :10，写随机落到其中一片，读时把 10 片的值加起来返回。
scenario_en: Key sharding splits a hot write key into views:video123:1 through :10; each write lands on a random shard and a read sums all ten values.
q: 哪类写操作不能用这种拆分方式承接？
q_en: Which kind of write cannot be absorbed by this splitting scheme?
options: 写多读少、最终只关心汇总值的指标上报，比如曝光量统计
可加和的计数器，比如视频播放量、点赞数这类单调累加
需要跨所有更新保持严格顺序、或要求多次更新整体原子生效的操作
允许读侧多花几毫秒把所有分片聚合起来的统计值，比如实时排行榜上的分数
options_en: Write-heavy, read-light metric reporting where only the aggregate matters, such as impression counts.
Summable counters such as video view counts or like counts that only ever increment.
Operations that need strict ordering across all updates, or several updates to take effect atomically together.
Statistics that can afford a few extra milliseconds aggregating every shard on read, such as live leaderboard scores.
why: 拆分把一次逻辑更新打散到多个节点，谁先落地无法保证，也没有跨片的原子提交；只有能分解再重组的操作（求和、计数）才成立，代价是读要聚合全部分片。
why_en: Sharding scatters one logical update across nodes with no guarantee of ordering and no cross-shard atomic commit, so it only works for operations you can decompose and recompose, like sums and counts. The cost is that reads must aggregate every shard.
optionExplanations: 错：只关心汇总值正是求和能还原的场景，拆分完全适用。
错：单调累加是可分解可重组的典型，10 片求和就是原值。
对：顺序和原子性都是跨片保证，而分片恰好把这两样拆没了。
错：读端多花几毫秒聚合，正是这套方案预期要付的代价。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect: caring only about the aggregate is exactly what summing restores, so splitting fits perfectly.
Incorrect: monotonic increments are the classic decomposable case; summing ten shards reproduces the value.
Correct: ordering and atomicity are cross-shard guarantees, and sharding is precisely what removes both.
Incorrect: spending a few extra milliseconds aggregating on read is the expected cost of this scheme.
